title: Go SDK streaming multiplexer: concurrency slots and graceful cancellation semantics
creator: Lucas Rivera
description: Implement a Go SDK streaming multiplexer that provides concurrency-limited client-side stream management, first-class support for context cancellation/timeouts, and clear retry semantics for transient errors. The goal is to make the Go streaming API ergonomic for common server patterns (partial outputs, reconnects, intermittent network errors) while preserving predictable resource usage (goroutine and buffer limits) and straightforward user code patterns (for loops / iterators).
background: Customer and internal workloads have surfaced two recurring problems: 1) naive streaming helpers spawn unbounded goroutines or buffers when callers start many streams concurrently, causing OOM and CPU spikes; 2) callers are confused about how context cancellation interacts with in-flight partial messages, retries, and backoff. Several existing tickets touch similar themes but focus on deadline normalization or resumable sessions; this work designs an API-level multiplexer and a set of cancellation/timeout primitives for the Go SDK that make those problems easier to avoid.
design_decisions: Introduce a StreamMultiplexer type that accepts a concurrency limit (slots) and an optional per-request deadline-normalizer. The multiplexer is a client-side coordinator, not a server-side protocol change.

Cancellation model: context.Context remains the single source-of-truth. The SDK will expose a lightweight StreamHandle with Cancel() for ergonomic cases but will propagate the underlying context to RPC stubs so server requests can be canceled immediately.

Partial message handling: provide two delivery modes: 'deliver-as-received' (channel of proto chunks) and 'aggregate-with-timeout' (combine chunks into higher-level messages with a flush timeout). Default to 'deliver-as-received' for minimal surprises.

Retries: only idempotent or client-declared retryable streams are retried automatically. Retries will honor the original user context deadline; when a retry extends past the deadline the SDK will return a wrapped error indicating 'deadline exceeded during retry'.

Resource limits: buffered writes/readers use bounded channels; multiplexer fails-fast with a clear error if slots/buffers are exhausted, to avoid indefinite blocking and to make throttling visible to callers.

Backpressure: the multiplexer tracks downstream consumer lag and exposes a simple metrics hook (consumer_lag) and an opt-in blocking mode where writes block into a bounded queue until the consumer catches up.

Ergonomics: provide two high-level helpers: StreamIterator(ctx, req) which returns a channel-like iterator that obeys ctx cancellations, and StreamCallback(ctx, req, fn) which calls fn for each received message and handles panic-safety and cancellation propagation.

Compatibility: keep public function names compact and avoid introducing major surface changes that break existing integrations; helpers are additive and the raw streaming client remains available for advanced users.
implementation_plan: Spike: prototype multiplexer skeleton with in-memory fake transport and unit tests for slot exhaustion and cancellation propagation (3d).
Core lib: implement StreamMultiplexer, StreamHandle, and the two delivery modes. Add bounded buffer config and metrics hooks (5d).
Retries: add retry coordinator with idempotency checks and deadline-aware backoff (2d).
Ergonomic wrappers: StreamIterator and StreamCallback helpers + examples (2d).
Docs and examples: write concise README, Go example that shows cancellation of a long-lived chat stream, and snippet for using multiplexer in server-side fanout (2d).
Integration tests: simulate flaky network, server-close mid-message, and ensure proper error surface and no goroutine leaks (3d).
Benchmarks: throughput and memory usage with high concurrency (1000 concurrent streams) vs baseline helper (2d).
Review & iterate: incorporate feedback from SDK owners and infra (2d).
acceptance_criteria: Public API added under internal/go/redwood/streammux with stable naming and tests covering cancellation propagation
No regression in existing streaming client tests; add leak tests asserting goroutine count returns to baseline within 5s of cancel
Benchmarks demonstrate bounded memory usage under 1K concurrent ephemeral streams and graceful failure when slots are exhausted
Retry behavior documented and exercised in unit tests: retries do not bypass caller deadlines and return clear error types
Example added to repo: examples/go/streaming_multiplexer demonstrating iterator and callback usage with cancellation
Design doc and PR reviewed by runtime and SDK leads, with explicit signoff on default buffer sizes and retry policy
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Kickoff meeting with SDK and runtime teams. Agreed on multiplexer concept and that context.Context is canonical cancellation source. (Lucas)
2026-03-07: Prototype spike complete. Simple multiplexer with slot counting and bounded channels. Found two race windows on cancel+retry transitions; added tests to reproduce. (Maya)
2026-03-09: Draft API landed in branch: github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/tree/stream-mux-spike. Early feedback: prefer explicit SlotReservation object over returning bool from Acquire(). (Aaron)
2026-03-10: Implemented StreamIterator helper and an example that cancels via context.WithTimeout. Local leak tests pass for the basic flow. (Maya)

2026-03-12: Added deadline-aware retry coordinator prototype and unit tests for 'deadline exceeded during retry' scenario. Preparing PR for internal review. Observed ~30% mem reduction against naive helper in microbenchmark. (Lucas)
qa_notes: Add goroutine-leak unit test: record runtime.NumGoroutine before and after a cancel+wait and assert within 5 goroutines of baseline after 2s.
Test combinations: immediate cancel before first message, cancel during aggregation flush, cancel during backoff retry, and context deadline shorter than retry backoff.
Validate behavior with both delivery modes; ensure aggregated mode still cancels promptly and does not swallow partial messages.
Run stress harness with 1K concurrent synthetic streams, each generating 50 messages; monitor heap and CPU for 30s.
review_feedback: 2026-03-11 - Priya Nair (runtime): Prefer opt-in blocking backpressure mode rather than implicit blocking so we don't deadlock customers' long-lived goroutines.
2026-03-11 - Aaron Kim (sdk): Suggest exposing metrics hooks via functional options instead of a global registry to keep package-level imports minimal.
2026-03-12 - Security (Jen Park): Confirmed no new privileged operations. Suggested adding a small guidance blurb about avoiding sending secrets over streaming requests in examples.
2026-03-12 - PM (Ravi Gupta): Request that the examples include a realistic chat use-case and an enterprise repair-case showing dedicated capacity fallback.
notes: Default slot count will be conservative (16) to avoid surprising memory growth; make it configurable via functional options.
We will not attempt resumable/offline session semantics in this ticket; that is scoped to a later project to avoid scope creep.
Documented tradeoffs: aggressive retries can amplify transient outages when many clients retry simultaneously; recommend jittered exponential backoff and global backoff coordination later.
